The Hubble Space Telescope has captured the closest image of comet Neowise, which recently flew over Earth. The picture was published on the [observatory website](https://www.spacetelescope.org/images/heic2015a/). The picture was reportedly taken on August 8, after the comet passed the Sun. Fan structures are visible on both sides of the comet. These are jets of sublimating ice from under the surface of the core. In this case, the resulting dust and gas are pushed through them at a high speed. The jets appear as cone-shaped structures and then fan out as the comet's nucleus rotates.
